prompt:
DIRECTION-LOCKED MOTION from a verified same-NPC view. IMAGE2 is the SAME NPC manually inspected NORTHWEST directional neutral enlarged nearest8x, the EXACT camera/identity/physical-hand calibration to preserve in every frame. IMAGE3 is the SAME directional neutral RAW; costume and prop detail only. All three images are in the target direction. No Southeast sheet is an input. Preserve this own neutral head, robe, tools and physical handedness throughout all18poses; never swivel to front or Southeast to display a gesture.

Physical handedness: Wooden sword in anatomical RIGHT hand (screen-left FRONT, screen-right BACK), left hand at rest. Keep wrist cloth and upright short hair. Do not exchange sword hand or add metal blade.

Use case: real sprite animation production. Produce one transparent RGBA source sheet for this same accepted NPC: exactly6columns x3rows,18separated complete full-body poses. Request1536x1536. No labels, grid, text, scene, floor, shadow, FX, aura or particles. Each pose and every prop pixel must have generous clear alpha gutter, consistent column centers and row boot ground lines. Do not clip or touch neighboring poses. Row1 idle6, row2 talk6, row3 profession6. Row1frame1 is directional neutral calibration; one source-wide scale is measured from this neutral later. All other poses preserve physical scale; no per-pose bbox fitting. Native human standing body80px, base64x96/foot32,88; motion96x96/foot48,88 adds transparent padding only. Skull/main hair around half standing height, short torso/legs and broad crisp few-tone pixel clusters. Frame6 of each row should settle to its own directional frame1 neutral; this is a generation intent, not a claim of pixel-equal end frames.

IMAGE1 is the actual live Wang Lin Pixel02 neutral in the TARGET direction enlarged nearest8x: PRIMARY human anatomy, broad pixel treatment, material shading, camera and native scale. IMAGE2 is the SAME NPC manually inspected NORTHWEST directional neutral enlarged nearest8x, the EXACT camera/identity/physical-hand calibration to preserve in every frame. IMAGE3 is the SAME directional neutral RAW; costume and prop detail only. All three images are in the target direction. No Southeast sheet is an input. Preserve this own neutral head, robe, tools and physical handedness throughout all18poses; never swivel to front or Southeast to display a gesture.

NPC Phùng Dã / NPC-HN-DISCIPLE-SWORD. Preserve compact upright spiked dark hair, adult competitive face, grey-green robe, earthy red-brown wrist/belt cloth and scratched short wooden training sword. No metal blade, enlarged weapon, armor or changed hairstyle. Large head and compact limbs remain his own accepted proportions.

ALL18poses remain NORTHWEST back-left three-quarter facing screen up-left, identical rear camera and body axes to IMAGE1. Show the back-left view throughout all18poses. Back hair, shoulders and robe dominate; do not reveal a front face, both eyes, front chest or palms through the torso. Held objects at front waist are naturally partly or fully hidden. Visible motion uses slight head inclination, shoulder/forearm changes and naturally exposed prop edges, never relocation of front-held props to the back.

Prop continuity in every row: Same small scratched wooden sword stays in the original physical holding hand for all18poses, low and clear of face. No dropped sword, hand swap, duplicated blade or trail. A low guard may briefly bring blade across lower waist as in the accepted pilot, but no overhead pose, attack arc or lunge.

Rear profession occlusion: Keep the same physical sword hand/flank; far-hand weapon can be partly occluded behind body. Low guard is in front of lower waist, not mysteriously across his visible back. In direct North communicate glance by slight head incline and wrist/shoulder change, without revealing a face or moving the sword to a different hand.

ROW IDLE6: frame1: Directional neutral calibration with both boots planted; frame2: Small inhalation in shoulders/cloth only; frame3: Slight sleeve/shoulder breathing change; frame4: Gentle exhalation without full-body bob or scaling; frame5: Subtle blink where eyes are actually visible, otherwise a settled shoulder/hair detail; frame6: Return to same source frame1 directional neutral.

ROW TALK6: frame1: Same directional standing neutral; frame2: Subtle speaking breath at shoulder/neck, mouth remains occluded where camera hides it; frame3: Restrained head inclination/nod, keeping the same back or back-quarter view; frame4: Small shoulder/neck speaking change while head nod begins to settle; frame5: Return head and shoulders; all low resting hands and props retained; frame6: Return to same source frame1 directional neutral.

ROW PROFESSION6: frame1: Directional standing rest neutral, same wooden sword lowered; frame2: Subtly correct the existing sword grip without changing physical holding hand; frame3: Make a small holding-wrist angle/low guard correction below chest; sword remains readable; frame4: Incline head slightly toward the same wooden sword tip without turning body or camera; frame5: Relax wrist and begin returning the sword to its original directional angle; frame6: Return to the same directional frame1 standing rest neutral.

Hair/robe/back construction is the minimal continuation of accepted identity: no extra emblems, pouches, decorations, hidden weapons, embroidery or face redesign. Motion is stationary with stable boots and genuine small pose changes; no six static duplicate images, full-body bobbing/scaling or camera rotation. Any naturally lower bounds while looking down remain natural, not normalized. New view/action is a candidate for review; owner acceptance of Southeast does not approve seven new views or runtime.
